title: Before I was formed (Berakhot 17a)
hook: Rava's Yom Kippur prayer: before I was formed I was nothing, and now I am as if unformed
tomorrow: the scholar or the farmer: who did more today?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sages' own prayers, and Mar's private line that ended up in everyone's siddur. Today, one sage's own words about himself.

College essay advice, every fall: sell yourself. Name your wins. Take up space. Now here's a sentence from the Talmud that walks the other way, and it's strange on purpose. Rava, a sage with students and a name, ended his prayer like this: before I was formed, I was not worthy, and now that I have been formed, it's as if I had not been formed. So how can a grown man call himself unformed?
screen: `SELL YOURSELF.` → `RAVA: AS IF UNFORMED.` → `HOW CAN THAT BE?`

segments.voice: Here's the rest of it, in plain words. Dust I am in my life, all the more so in my death. Here I am before You like a vessel full of shame. May it be Your will that I not sin again, and what I have sinned, wipe away in Your mercy, but not through suffering. The Talmud adds that Rav Hamnuna Zuti said these same words on Yom Kippur. Now the puzzle. One traditional reading solves it like this. Before I existed, nothing required me to exist. Now that I'm here, I haven't yet become what I was made for, so it's as if I'm still unfinished. It isn't a sentence about being worthless. It's a sentence about being in progress. Then the second strange line: dust I am in my life. Rava is alive, and he says dust anyway. He's standing where Abraham stood, who told God he was "but dust and ashes," in Genesis: "who am but dust and ashes." Here's what's worth telling a friend tonight. This humble prayer still asks for something big: wipe it away, and spare me the suffering. The humility doesn't shrink the request. It's what makes the honest request possible. So the essay coach and Rava aren't really arguing. One is talking to an admissions office. Rava is talking to God.
screen: `DUST IN MY LIFE.` · `UNFINISHED, NOT WORTHLESS.` · `LIKE ABRAHAM: DUST AND ASHES.` · `HUMBLE, AND STILL ASKING.` · then, large: `DUST WHILE ALIVE.`

segments.voice: Say one humble sentence out loud, softly, that's true about you right now: where you're still unfinished, still learning. Rava said his to God; yours can go wherever it goes. Then let it stay in the room without fixing it.
screen: `ONE HUMBLE SENTENCE.` · `OUT LOUD, SOFTLY.` · `LET IT STAY.`

segments.voice: Before I was formed. Rava's prayer after his prayer: not yet what he was made to be, dust in his life, and still asking for mercy.
Pocket line: dust while alive, unfinished and still asking. Thirteen of fifty, and the tractate keeps going.
